reason: The narrative centers on Cain and Abel, two working brothers—one a shepherd (רֹעֵה צֹאן) and one a farmer (עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה)—as the primary characters. The story focuses on their labor, their offerings derived from their work, and the human emotions and conflicts that arise from their ordinary lives. The concerns of these regular, working people—their jealousy, anger, and the tragic murder—form the core of the narrative. While the narrator employs an omniscient third-person voice that includes divine perspective (which is characteristic of biblical narrative), the story is fundamentally grounded in and centered upon the lives and experiences of these working people.
